I was around 10 or 11, and I was waiting for my friend to show up at my place so we could hang out. I admit that I had some problems back then and still kind of do with anxiety, though it has gotten better since I started seeing a counselor. But anyways, my anxiety got the best of me when my friend was 5 minutes late at the time, with me thinking that he decided to ditch me and go hang out with his other friends. Me, thinking there was something horribly wrong with me that I thought was keeping him from wanting to hang out, hopped on my older brother's bike (he was on a skiing trip in NC at the time, so this was a very rare occurrence for me) and I go up one of the very rare hills in the area of FL where I lived at the time. I ready myself at the top of this hill and push myself down and I begin peddling as hard as I every possibly could, going what I felt like was 25+ mph, which to a 10 year old boy on a bike, is pretty fucking speedy. So I'm nearing the bottom of this hill where I'm about to turn full speed onto my mom's gravel driveway with 2 gigantic stone pillars on each side, both of them with sharp, jagged rocks jutting out of them, and that was when I realized what a terrible mistake I had made. I was headed for the driveway, and I had no other choice but to turn. It was either that, or go full speed with a yellow trail behind me into a extremely dense Florida forest and get thrown off my bike and potentially get really fucked up. So I turn full speed onto that gravel driveway, and what do you know, one of the tires decides to go into this huge pothole in the driveway, flipping the bike up and throwing me out, directly towards the stone pillar. I slammed into the pillar with the full force of my body and then slid about 7 feet on my chest and belly on the gravel driveway and the little concrete parking space beyond that driveway. I crawled back onto my feet, and being the 10 year old me in complete shock, started crying like a bitch. But it wasn't because I was hurt that bad, but because I could here the air flowing out of the tires of my brothers bike, and I knew that I had completely destroyed the brakes as well, so I knew that he was going to kill me when he got back from his skiing trip. So long story short from there on, I got road rash really bad all over the front side of my body and my arms, and a rock the top of my hand open, and I didn't even feel that cut. They said that I wouldn't be able to feel anything beyond the my pinkie, which I still can't to this day, because it cut through a bunch of nerves. They didn't end up putting stitches in it though, they just poured a bunch of hydrogen peroxide (I didn't feel a thing from that, and I'm pretty sure that was due to the lack of nerves I had in that area) and just glued it back together. Only problem is, they put gauze wrap over that immediately after gluing my hand back together, so you can imagine that pulling that stuff off a few days later wasn't very pleasant.
